conviction_note: ROKU is a pending-merger stock: Fox's definitive agreement (2026-06-15) pays a fixed $96 cash plus 0.9693 FOXA per share, with no collar, shareholder votes passed 2026-10-14, and only the DOJ's HSR second request still open. Over the window the price is about 0.39 x FOXA's move plus any change in a roughly $0.9-1.2 spread. Roku's Q3 release comes with no call and no outlook, and it can only move deal-break odds, which it barely touches. The sum of findings (+0.1) and the scaled number (0, p_up 50) agree. Both are much smaller than the 3.31% option-implied move, because the options are illiquid (OI 3,133, ATM spread 26% of mid) and 20-day realised vol is 12.3% annualised.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue $1.41bn (+16.7% y/y), EPS $0.53, per 24/7 Wall St preview 2026-10-27 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/rokus-q3-earnings-why-the-fox-merger-changes-everything-for-roku-stock-nov-2). Single source and the company gives no guidance, so the bar is unsourced to a company guide and every print-related size is capped small. The bar the stock actually trades against is the deal value: $96 + 0.9693 x FOXA. At FOXA $63.18 (Yahoo, 2026-11-02 13:26 ET) that is $157.24, against ROKU at $156.04-156.38.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 10.4M shares, 3.7 days to cover, settlement 2026-08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/roku/short-interest/). Equibles shows 10.6M and 4.3 days for late August (https://equibles.com/stocks/roku/shortinterest). I found no October settlement because Nasdaq's API returned 503. In a stock+cash merger, arbs are typically long ROKU and short FOXA, so the short sits in FOXA, not ROKU; ROKU short interest is not crowded. The 25-delta skew of +10.2 vol points is the deal-break tail: a fall toward the unaffected ~$119 (the $160 price was a 34% premium). It is not a statement about the print. Put/call OI is 0.71 on only 3,133 contracts.

findings.finding: Deal structure caps the print. Fox pays $96.00 cash plus a fixed 0.9693 FOXA shares per ROKU share, with no collar or walk-away tied to Fox's price (424B3). Both shareholder votes passed on 2026-10-14. The outside date is 2027-06-14 with automatic regulatory extensions. ROKU's value over the window is therefore about $96 + 0.9693 x FOXA, and the stock element is about 39% of the $157 value. Roku's Q3 numbers can only reach the price through deal-break odds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's seven reactions (median |move| 8.5%) are all pre-deal standalone prints, and the sweep marks the history untrustworthy. The only post-announcement print, 2026-08-06, moved +2.03%. On the deal-era tape, 20-day realised vol is 12.3% annualised (~0.8% a day).
findings.why_not_priced: This is not unpriced. It is the frame that says the print is nearly irrelevant. If the market treated this as a normal earnings event, the stock would not sit $1 under deal value with 12% realised vol. The 3.31% straddle comes from an illiquid chain, not from a priced print risk.
findings.independence: Both the Fox and Roku Form 425 filings (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001428439/000114036126025255/ef20076241_form425.htm) give the same terms. Roku's own Q3 date notice says no call and no outlook because of the transaction (https://finviz.com/news/404215/roku-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-on-nov-2).

findings.finding: The spread to deal value roughly halved on 2026-11-02, before the entry close. With FOXA at 63.24 and ROKU at 155.12 on Oct 30, the gap was about $2.18, and it was $1.9-2.2 every session from Oct 21 to Oct 30. On Nov 2 at 13:26 ET it was about $1.20 (FOXA 63.18, ROKU 156.04), or $0.86 at the baseline seal price of 156.38. The tightening followed Fox's 08:30 ET call, where Lachlan Murdoch said all shareholder and foreign regulatory approvals were in hand, Fox was 'continuing to work cooperatively with the DOJ' and aimed to close 'as soon as we can'. Fox also restarted buybacks, though the CFO said not to link them to deal timing. A residual spread of about 0.6-0.8% leaves almost no upside from further tightening. A partial give-back is the more likely small move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print on the spread. On Nov 2 the spread moved about $1, or 0.6% of ROKU, on Fox's call language alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced at the entry close; the tightening happened intraday on Nov 2. I file it because the residual spread sets the asymmetry for the window: little room up, some room for a give-back if the market rereads 'work cooperatively with the DOJ' as no timeline.
findings.independence: Fox call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/02/fox-foxa-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/) for the cause. FOXA prices from a separate chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FOXA?range=1mo&interval=1d). The ROKU daily dates in the Yahoo output appear shifted by a day (they show Sunday Oct 25 and Nov 1), so I aligned them using the 13:26 ET timestamp that matches FOXA.

findings.finding: Counterparty read-through: Fox's quarter to 2026-09-30, reported 2026-11-02 before the open, showed advertising revenue up 47% on the World Cup, political ads and Tubi digital growth. That points to a strong political and CTV ad quarter for Roku's Platform segment (Q2 Platform +25%) against a revenue consensus of only +16.7% y/y ($1.41bn). A Roku beat slightly raises the standalone value under the deal, which trims break-risk downside. It cannot lift the stock above the deal value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Post-deal, the Q2 print (EPS $1.08 vs $0.56 consensus, revenue +21.9%) moved +2.03% on 2026-08-06, when the spread was still wide (implied value $161.16 on Aug 27 against a lower price). With the spread now ~$1, the same beat has less room.
findings.why_not_priced: A Roku revenue beat is likely and nobody prices it, because under a fixed-ratio deal it does not matter. If the market cared, ROKU would trade at a premium to deal value or with a wide spread. It does neither.
findings.independence: A proxy: Fox's own ad mix, not Roku's number. Q2 Platform +25% from the 24/7 preview (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/rokus-q3-earnings-why-the-fox-merger-changes-everything-for-roku-stock-nov-2) points the same way. The consensus is single-source, so the size is capped.

findings.finding: FOXA linkage: 0.9693 FOXA is about $61 of ROKU's ~$157 value, so ROKU's window move is about 0.39 x FOXA's Nov 3 move, the second session after Fox's Nov 2 pre-market print. FOXA was flat on the print day (63.24 on Oct 30 to 63.18 intraday Nov 2) despite adjusted EBITDA up 54% and adjusted EPS of $2.54 against $1.51. That gives no directional lean for day two.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. The mechanism is arithmetic from the fixed exchange ratio.
findings.why_not_priced: This finding sets the scale of the move, not its direction. It is the main reason abs_move_pct sits near 0.9% rather than at the option-implied 3.3%.
findings.independence: Exchange ratio from the 424B3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001754301/000119312526377686/d94663d424b3.htm). FOXA results from the Fox 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001754301/000162828026068663/foxearningsreleaseq127.htm). Shares the FOXA price document with finding 2.

outside_window.finding: DOJ HSR second request, issued 2026-09-08, still open. Fox gave the DOJ more time (Law360/CPI, 2026-08-10). The review focuses on self-preferencing on Roku's home screen, ad data and Frndly TV. Clearance or a challenge is the real catalyst for the spread, roughly +1 point or a fall toward ~$119 unaffected. No decision is scheduled inside the window, and Fox still guides to H1 2027 'as soon as we can'.

baseline_tension: The positive skew (+10.2) and the stock 2.3% off its 52-week high, 88% above its low, are a merger-arb price. The skew is the deal-break tail, not a view on the print. Nothing found cuts against it, and nothing found gives a direction for the window.
